newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France wants EU action on VAT, company, savings tax.
newsitem.headline: France wants EU action on VAT, company, savings tax.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday France wanted European Union action to tackle discrepancies on Value Added Tax, company tax and savings taxes.

He told a news conference after a meeting of EU finance ministers that a "code of good conduct" would not be enough to eliminate unfair competition due to different tax regimes inside the European Union.

One issue particularly important to France, which relies heavily on VAT (sales tax) for government revenues, was "VAT leakages" due to the fact that goods brought in one EU country for use in another were not subject to VAT when they were sold.
He gave no details on how this question should be resolved.
Europe would also have to look at taxation of companies and corporate capital gains, and savings taxes, he said.
Luxembourg, which has just taken over the EU presidency, has pledged to hold talks on taxation during the next six months.
